subject: computable Scott analysis
statement: The paper develops two new coding tools, the Belligerent Pairs Theorem and Belligerent Jump Inversion Theorem, which reflect complexity level 2α information in computable structures.

subject: jump inversion
statement: The paper extends Harrison-Trainor's finite unfriendly jump inversion uniformly throughout the computable ordinals.

subject: computable Scott sentences
statement: The paper determines the oracle needed to compute a Π_α Scott sentence for every computable infinite ordinal α.

subject: back-and-forth relations
statement: The paper proves that bounds on oracle complexity for back-and-forth relations are sharp and resolves a question of Chen, Gonzalez, and Harrison-Trainor.

subject: sparse random graphs
statement: The paper proves an MSO_2 zero-one law for very sparse Erdős-Rényi graphs after component-order pruning.

subject: component pruning conditions
statement: The paper shows that the term f(n)log f(n) cannot simply be omitted, as star components occur at first-order-visible Poisson thresholds.

subject: bond percolation on tori
statement: The paper establishes first-order limit laws for bond percolation on the discrete torus T_L^d with distinct behavior in polynomial regimes.

subject: MSO on tori
statement: The paper shows that MSO_1 detects the parity of the torus side length through bipartiteness, obstructing monadic convergence.

subject: polymorphic cumulative universes
statement: The paper proposes a new fuss-free generalised algebraic presentation for polymorphic cumulative universes without intricate universe coercions.

subject: universe coercions
statement: The paper proves equivalence to coherent universe coercions by means of a normalisation theorem.

subject: datatype descriptions
statement: The paper describes and implements an extension of the universe hierarchy with a judgemental notion of datatype description.

subject: hereditarily finite multisets
statement: The paper introduces two first-order theories of hereditarily finite multisets: WF^- and F^-.

subject: mutual interpretability
statement: The paper proves WF^- is mutually interpretable with Robinson's theory R and F^- with Robinson arithmetic Q.

subject: essential undecidability
statement: The paper proves that F^- is essentially undecidable.

subject: ordered pair recovery
statement: The paper shows that order is recoverable from bare multiplicity via the term π(x,y) = <x> ∪ <x> ∪ <y>, yielding an interpretation of tree theory.

subject: universal homogeneous Abelian groups
statement: The paper characterizes Abelian groups that are universal and homogeneous for finitely co-generated, finite, and cardinality-bounded groups.

subject: ray spaces
statement: The paper provides a combinatorial characterization for pairs of order-theoretic trees with homeomorphic ray spaces.

subject: topological games
statement: The paper introduces a transfinite topological game that characterizes ray spaces through winning strategies.

subject: end spaces
statement: The paper establishes that scattered property equals end space property for subspaces of continuum cardinality.

subject: ray space products
statement: The paper determines that ray spaces in some classes fail to have their product with non-discrete spaces as ray spaces.

subject: quasiminimal pregeometry structures
statement: The paper shows that expansions with dense codense unary predicates can be axiomatized with a single L_{ω1ω}(Q)-sentence.

subject: ω-stable expansions
statement: The paper shows that both expansions are ω-stable.

subject: independence in expansions
statement: The paper provides a natural notion of independence in the expansion for H-structures and for beautiful pairs when the underlying structure is modular.

subject: Coding Conception
statement: The paper proposes the Coding Conception of ordinals and sets, based solely on Cantor's three generating principles.

subject: theory of ordinals
statement: The paper establishes that SC^{reg} is the metamathematically correct theory of the ordinals and is bi-interpretable with ZFGC^+.

subject: Power Set Dichotomy
statement: The paper proves that the Power Set Dichotomy is unavoidable, even under potentialism.

subject: set theory fragments
statement: The paper concludes that ZFC^-+'every cardinal has a successor' is the only philosophically uncontroversial common fragment of any true set theory.

subject: tall Borel Ramsey ideals
statement: The paper proves that a tall Borel Ramsey ideal admits no countable local reading.

subject: quotients of Ramsey ideals
statement: The paper proves that below every positive set, a tall Borel Ramsey ideal is not a countable intersection of topologically represented ideals.

subject: weakly selective ideals
statement: The paper proves that a weakly selective q^+ ideal admits no positive ED_{fin}-carrier.

subject: tame μ-AECs of modules
statement: The paper shows that under suitable syntactic assumptions, all tame μ-AECs of R-modules are almost stable.

subject: pure submodule relation
statement: The paper proves that (R-Mod, ≤_{pp}^μ) has a stable independence relation and is a stable and tame μ-AEC.

subject: μ-AECs with summand refinement
statement: The paper proves almost stability of all μ-AECs where the embedding refines the direct summand relation with strong coherence.

subject: p-adic Levi-Civita fields
statement: The paper introduces p-adic Levi-Civita fields as subfields of p-adic Hahn fields.

subject: Urysohn universal ultrametric spaces
statement: The paper proves that Levi-Civita valued fields are isometric to R-Urysohn universal ultrametric spaces for prescribed subgroups and fields.

subject: haloed valued fields
statement: The paper proves that complete valued fields with infinite residue fields are haloed and universal for separable ultrametric spaces.

subject: cardinal invariants
statement: The paper proves b < cof(UN) and non(N) = non(UN) < cof(UN) in ZFC for universally null sets.

subject: cofinality of universally null
statement: The paper proves, assuming add(N) = c, that cof(UN) = d_c.

subject: cardinal inequalities
statement: The paper proves the consistency of add(UN) < cov(UN) < non(UN) < cof(UN).

subject: Los-Tarski preservation theorem
statement: The paper refutes Purdy's claim that a Los-Tarski preservation theorem holds for the fluted fragment.

subject: fluted fragment expressivity
statement: The paper constructs a fluted sentence of quantifier rank three that is preserved under extensions but not equivalent to any existential fluted sentence.

subject: topological square of S4.1
statement: The paper finds the axiomatization for the topological square of S4.1.

subject: modal logic S4.1
statement: The paper proves the finite model property and decidability for the topological square of S4.1.

subject: Constant Domain Axiom
statement: The paper shows how constant domain intuitionistic logic's semantics in presheaf toposes fits topos theory via covert Hausdorff objects.

subject: CD objects
statement: The paper shows that CD objects form a Boolean pretopos in any topos.

subject: intuitionistic dynamic logics
statement: The paper develops the mathematical theory of five intuitionistic dynamic logics with modalities and fixed point operators.

subject: axiomatizations and sequent calculi
statement: The paper develops sound and complete Hilbert-style axiomatizations and cyclic sequent calculi for intuitionistic dynamic logics.

subject: intuitionistic linear temporal logic
statement: The paper develops a sound and complete axiomatization for intuitionistic linear temporal logic, answering a long-standing open question.

subject: effectively zero-knowledge proofs
statement: The paper reformulates effectively zero-knowledge proofs in the language of logic.

subject: proof complexity generators
statement: The paper shows how effectively zero-knowledge proofs can be converted to genuinely zero-knowledge proofs using proof complexity generators.

subject: game semantics
statement: The paper establishes a fully abstract correlation between base-extension semantics and Hyland-Ong game semantics.

subject: proof-theoretic semantics
statement: The paper gives a sound and complete base-extension semantics for intuitionistic propositional logic.

subject: uniform convexity
statement: The paper derives new formulas for quantities involved in the study of uniformly convex spaces, linear and nonlinear.

subject: reconstruction of varieties
statement: The paper extends Kollár-Lieblich-Olsson-Sawin theorems on reconstructing varieties from Zariski topological spaces to arbitrary quasi-projective varieties in arbitrary characteristic.

subject: model-theoretic algebraic geometry
statement: The paper employs a general model-theoretic setting known as the Zilber trichotomy for ACF-relics for algebro-geometric reconstruction problems.
